cards.title: Needs vs Wants: The golden financial filter
facts: A 'need' is essential for survival, health, and basic education; a 'want' is a desire that can be delayed or skipped.
Distinguishing between needs and wants is the single most important habit for avoiding lifelong debt.
do: Pause 24 hours before buying non-essential items to curb impulse spending
Ask yourself: 'What happens if I do not buy this today?'
Cover food, books, and essential bus fare before spending on snacks or merchandise
dont: Never label temporary peer cravings as urgent life needs
Never spend emergency savings on entertainment or trendy clothing

myths.statement: If you desire something intensely, that automatically turns it into a financial need.
myths.truth: Emotional intensity does not change necessity. Needs sustain life and daily function; wants are upgrades.

quiz.q: Which of the following is genuinely classified as a 'need' for a school student?
options: A limited-edition gaming skin
Prescription spectacles or standard school uniform
Brand-new trendy sneakers when current shoes fit well
Eating out at a fast-food cafe every afternoon
quiz.explanation: Medical items, nutrition, and essential school requirements are basic needs; luxury brand upgrades are wants.

situations: While shopping with friends at {at}, {name} sees a stylish imported jacket on discount that everyone praises, but {name} only has pocket money saved for upcoming textbook purchases.
scenario.question: How should {name} decide whether to purchase it?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Prioritize necessary school textbooks as a core need over the jacket
rubric.note: Ensures essential obligations are fulfilled without financial distress.

rubric.point: Implement a 24-hour cooling-off period to evaluate true value
Recognize the jacket as a temporary want that can be saved for later
rubric.keys: want not need|save for it later|delay gratification

sources.name: Reserve Bank of India - Financial Education

cards.title: Budgeting your money: The 50/30/20 bucket method
facts: The 50/30/20 rule splits income: 50% for necessities, 30% for personal wants/fun, and 20% for future savings.
Budgeting does not mean depriving yourself of fun; it ensures you enjoy today while securing tomorrow.
do: Divide any received allowance or gift money into three distinct jars or envelopes
Always deposit the 20% savings first ('pay yourself first')
Track total expenses in a pocket notebook or mobile ledger at least once a week
dont: Never spend 100% of money received on the day you receive it
Never dip into the savings bucket for impulsive weekend outings

myths.statement: Budgeting means you are never allowed to spend money on entertainment or fun.
myths.truth: A healthy budget explicitly reserves 30% for guilt-free fun so you don't burn out or binge spend.

quiz.q: According to the 50/30/20 budgeting rule, what proportion of allowance should be directed to future savings?
options: At least 20%
quiz.explanation: Allocating 20% toward long-term savings builds an emergency cushion and teaches compound wealth.

situations: {name} receives 500 rupees as monthly pocket money at {at}. Friends urge {name} to spend it all immediately on milkshakes and video games.
scenario.question: How should {name} allocate this money systematically?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Set aside at least 100 rupees (20%) immediately into a savings jar
rubric.note: Secures the savings component before any spending occurs.

rubric.point: Allocate 50% for actual requirements like stationery and bus fare
Allow a planned portion for social fun without exceeding the budget

cards.title: Unit pricing: Spotting deceptive supermarket packaging
facts: Bigger boxes or family packs are not always cheaper; manufacturers sometimes price larger volumes higher per gram.
Unit pricing measures cost per standard metric (e.g., price per 100g or per liter), exposing true costs.
do: Calculate the price per 100g or per piece before assuming the 'jumbo pack' is a discount
Look at the lowest and highest shelves in grocery aisles where cheaper unpromoted brands sit
Check expiry and manufacturing dates before buying bulk perishables
dont: Never trust flashy 'Buy 2 Get 1 Free' stickers without comparing single-pack unit costs
Never purchase excess perishable groceries just because of a bulk offer

myths.statement: Larger package sizes are always guaranteed to be cheaper per gram than small packs.
myths.truth: Retailers frequently exploit this assumption; unit price calculations regularly reveal smaller packs are cheaper.

quiz.q: How do you determine which brand of cereal or detergent offers the genuinely lowest price?
options: Check which box has the brightest cartoon character
Calculate the price per 100 grams or millilitres
Pick whichever box says 'Special Value Pack'
Buy whichever is placed at eye level
quiz.explanation: Comparing price per standard unit (gram/ml) reveals exact mathematical value regardless of box size.

situations: At the grocery store at {at}, {name} sees Brand A selling 200g of biscuits for Rs 40 (Rs 20/100g) and a 'Giant Saver Pack' of 350g for Rs 84 (Rs 24/100g).
scenario.question: Which option should {name} choose and why?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Calculate price per 100g and discover the smaller pack is cheaper per unit
Reject the deceptive 'Giant Saver' claim
Check the expiry date on the shelf items before completing payment

dangerous: blindly buy giant pack assuming cheaper

sources.name: Department of Consumer Affairs, Government of India

cards.title: MRP laws and bill verification: Never overpay
facts: Maximum Retail Price (MRP) is the legal ceiling in India; charging even one rupee above MRP is a punishable offense under Legal Metrology laws.
Billing errors, duplicate scans, and unapplied promotional discounts occur regularly at checkout counters.
do: Always check the printed MRP on packaged bottles and snacks before handing over money
Review itemized printed bills line-by-line before leaving the store premises
Report vendors who charge extra for 'chilling' cold drinks to the National Consumer Helpline (1915)
dont: Never accept hand-written overcharges above the printed MRP
Never leave a store without collecting a printed tax invoice or cash receipt

myths.statement: Shopkeepers have legal permission to charge extra 5 rupees above MRP for keeping drinks in their refrigerator.
myths.truth: Under the Legal Metrology Act, MRP is all-inclusive of cooling, storage, and taxes. Overcharging is illegal.

quiz.q: What should you do if a vendor demands 5 rupees extra above the printed MRP for a cold bottle of juice?
options: Quietly pay whatever they demand
Point out the printed MRP and refuse to pay extra cooling charges
Threaten physical violence
Throw the bottle on the counter
quiz.explanation: By Indian law, MRP includes all taxes and retailer margins; cooling is an overhead cost the shopkeeper cannot charge extra for.

situations: At a tourist bus stand kiosk at {at}, {name} is handed a bottle of water with MRP Rs 20, but the shopkeeper insists on Rs 25 citing 'refrigeration fees'.
scenario.question: How should {name} handle this consumer situation?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Politely point out the printed MRP of Rs 20 and state cooling fees are legally included
Decline to purchase and find an authorized vendor if the seller insists on overcharging
rubric.note: Refuses to reward illicit retail extortion.
rubric.keys: refuse to pay extra|find honest vendor

rubric.point: Know that consumer complaints can be registered on National Consumer Helpline 1915

dangerous: pay the illegal markup without checking

cards.title: UPI PIN safety: Enter PIN only to SEND money
facts: Your UPI PIN (4 or 6 digits) is an authorization key to transfer money OUT of your bank account.
Receiving money via UPI, Google Pay, PhonePe, or Paytm NEVER requires entering your PIN, scanning a QR code, or clicking an approval link.
do: Remember the golden rule: UPI PIN is ONLY entered when debited/paying, NEVER to receive funds
Immediately decline any caller or buyer who asks you to 'enter PIN to collect cash prize'
Check the beneficiary account name on the confirmation screen before hitting submit
dont: NEVER enter your UPI PIN on forms sent via SMS, WhatsApp, or OLX chats
NEVER share your banking OTP or UPI PIN with bank managers or tech support

myths.statement: You must enter your UPI PIN to authenticate receiving cashback or money transfers from a buyer.
myths.truth: Receiving money is completely automatic and requires zero PIN entries. If prompted for a PIN, money is leaving your account.

quiz.q: A buyer on an online marketplace offers to pay you Rs 500 and sends a QR code saying 'Scan and enter PIN to receive payment'. What is happening?
options: It is a safe standard transaction
It is an advance payment feature
It is a scam designed to drain Rs 500 from your account
It verifies your identity
quiz.explanation: Scanning a QR code and entering a PIN always debits funds from your account, never credits it.

situations: {name} is selling an old bicycle on an online portal. A buyer at {at} claims to have sent Rs 2,000 and messages: 'Accept request and enter your UPI PIN to claim money.'
scenario.question: What should {name} do?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Refuse to enter the UPI PIN, recognizing that receiving money never requires a PIN
rubric.keys: never enter pin to receive|refuse request|scam attempt

rubric.point: Check account balance directly in the official banking app without clicking chat links
rubric.note: Verifies funds through secure independent channels.
rubric.keys: check banking app directly|do not click links

rubric.point: Block and report the fraudulent buyer profile immediately
rubric.note: Prevents further exploitation of community members.

dangerous: enter pin to test if money arrives

sources.name: Reserve Bank of India - Sachet Portal

cards.title: Minor savings accounts: Opening your first bank account
facts: Indian banks allow minors above age 10 to operate independent savings bank accounts (like SBI Pehla Kadam) with debit cards and checkbooks.
Holding a real bank account transitions youth from cash dependency to structured digital financial literacy.
do: Keep your physical debit card, CVV number, and ATM PIN strictly confidential
Memorize your 4-digit ATM PIN and never write it down on the card surface or slip
Check monthly bank passbook statements to verify account balance and interest earned
dont: Never let friends or strangers punch your ATM PIN on keypad screens
Never throw away ATM transaction slips without tearing them into tiny shreds

myths.statement: Minors in India are legally forbidden from holding bank accounts or using ATM debit cards.
myths.truth: Minors aged 10+ can operate savings accounts independently under RBI guidelines to cultivate financial discipline.

quiz.q: Where is the safest place to record your newly issued ATM debit card PIN?
options: Written on the back of the debit card with permanent marker
Stored in your head through memorization only
Posted on your study desk whiteboard
Shared in a family WhatsApp group
quiz.explanation: ATM PINs must only be memorized. Writing it down invites unauthorized physical withdrawals if the card is misplaced.

situations: {name} receives their first teenage debit card from their bank branch at {at}. A classmate asks to borrow the card to check how it works.
scenario.question: How should {name} safeguard the new banking card?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Firmly refuse to hand over the debit card or disclose the secret PIN
rubric.note: Establishes strict personal boundary around banking credentials.
rubric.keys: refuse to lend card|keep pin secret|memorize pin

rubric.point: Memorize the PIN and scratch or cover the 3-digit CVV on the back
Review monthly passbook statements with parents to track deposits

dangerous: post card photo on social media

sources.name: Reserve Bank of India Guidelines for Minor Accounts

cards.title: Compound interest: Earning interest on your interest
facts: Albert Einstein famously called compound interest the 'eighth wonder of the world': you earn returns on your initial principal AND on accumulated returns.
Time in the market is vastly more powerful than timing the market; starting at age 14 creates exponential growth compared to starting at age 30.
do: Start investing small amounts (even Rs 100/month via Recurring Deposit or PPF) as early as possible
Let your investments grow undisturbed over years rather than withdrawing small profits prematurely
Understand the Rule of 72: divide 72 by annual interest rate to find years needed to double money
dont: Never delay saving until your late twenties assuming small amounts don't matter
Never confuse high-risk gambling with long-term compound investing

myths.statement: To build substantial wealth through compounding, you must start with hundreds of thousands of rupees.
myths.truth: Compound growth relies on TIME and consistency, not large starting sums. Rs 500 invested monthly over decades creates massive wealth.

quiz.q: If an investment pays an 8% annual return, roughly how many years will it take to double your money according to the Rule of 72?
options: 2 years
9 years (72 divided by 8)
20 years
72 years
quiz.explanation: The Rule of 72 states 72 / 8 = 9 years to double your initial capital automatically.

situations: {name} at {at} receives Rs 2,000 birthday gift. Option A is spending it on trendy branded sneakers; Option B is depositing it in a long-term compound savings bond.
scenario.question: How should {name} evaluate this financial crossroads?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Recognize that early compounding allows small deposits to multiply exponentially over time
Calculate how leaving money untouched over years builds financial freedom
Choose to invest the majority while keeping a modest sum for a small celebratory treat
rubric.note: Strikes healthy balance between present reward and future security.

dangerous: blow all money on temporary shoes
borrow more to buy luxury goods

sources.name: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) - Investor Education

cards.title: Borrowing and lending: Preserving friendship and solvency
facts: Informal loans between friends and peers cause severe social anxiety, broken friendships, and awkward school dynamics.
Borrowing money for non-essential lifestyle wants creates toxic habits before adult life even begins.
do: Never borrow money to buy luxury items, treats, or impressionable outfits
If you must borrow for an emergency (like fare), set an exact repayment deadline and pay early
Only lend amounts you can afford to lose without destroying the friendship
dont: Never shy away from asking for your own money back when a promised deadline passes
Never guarantee or take loans on behalf of another student

myths.statement: Borrowing small amounts from peers every week to fund snacks is completely harmless.
myths.truth: Casual borrowing creates dependency, damages social trust, and blinds youth to their true spending habits.

quiz.q: What is the healthiest rule regarding lending money to classmates?
options: Lend your entire monthly allowance without asking when they will return it
Only lend small amounts you can comfortably afford not to get back, with clear repayment terms
Charge 50% weekly interest
Lend secretly without telling your parents
quiz.explanation: Clear agreements and conservative limits protect both personal finances and personal relationships.

situations: A close classmate at {at} asks {name} to lend Rs 300 to buy a video game, promising to repay 'sometime next month', but has an unpaid past debt.
scenario.question: How should {name} navigate this friendship situation?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Politely decline the loan, explaining that personal money is budgeted for other commitments
Remind the friend calmly about the previous unsettled amount
rubric.note: Holds friends accountable to past commitments.

rubric.point: Suggest free alternative games or ways they can earn the money directly
rubric.note: Offers constructive support without funding debt.

dangerous: lend money out of social guilt

cards.title: Pyramid schemes & fake returns: If it's too good to be true, it's fake
facts: No legitimate financial instrument guarantees 20%, 50%, or 100% returns in days or weeks; bank savings yield ~3-7% annually.
Multi-level marketing (MLM) and Telegram crypto bots recruit students by displaying fake rented supercars and fake screenshots.
do: Remember: High guaranteed returns with zero risk ALWAYS indicate an illegal Ponzi scam
Verify financial firms on official SEBI or RBI directories before trusting claims
Warn peers when a club or senior asks for 'entry fee' to recruit downlines
dont: NEVER invest money into Telegram trading signals or Instagram 'fund doubling' groups
NEVER recruit friends into schemes that pay commissions purely for enrolling new members

myths.statement: If a senior shows real bank account balance screenshots proving they doubled money in 3 days, the app must be genuine.
myths.truth: Balance screenshots are easily fabricated with inspect element or dummy apps to bait gullible recruits.

quiz.q: What is the universal hallmark of a fraudulent pyramid or Ponzi scheme?
options: Regulated by SEBI and audited annually
Promises guaranteed astronomical returns with no risk and rewards recruiting friends
Provides printed tax invoices for all transactions
Requires years of patient disciplined compounding
quiz.explanation: Guaranteed rapid profits paired with pressure to recruit friends is the textbook definition of an illegal pyramid scheme.

situations: A senior student invites {name} to a cafe at {at}, presenting an app: 'Deposit Rs 1,000 today, get Rs 2,000 next Monday, plus Rs 500 for every junior you sign up!'
scenario.question: How should {name} respond?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Identify this immediately as an illegal Ponzi / pyramid scheme and refuse to participate
Refuse to recruit classmates or risk personal savings
rubric.note: Protects peer community from financial harm.

rubric.point: Report the recruiting activity to school authorities or the RBI Sachet portal
rubric.note: Takes civic action to stop exploitation.

dangerous: convince best friends to join for bonus

sources.name: RBI Sachet Portal against Illegal Deposit Schemes

cards.title: Dark patterns: Deceptive tricks in shopping apps
facts: Dark patterns are user-interface tricks designed to manipulate you into spending money, such as fake countdown timers and stealth subscriptions.
The Ministry of Consumer Affairs has legally prohibited 13 deceptive dark patterns in Indian e-commerce.
do: Look out for pre-ticked checkboxes adding travel insurance, charity donations, or subscriptions
Ignore flashing 'Only 2 items left at this price!' banners designed to induce synthetic panic
Always check the final checkout total before clicking the final 'Pay' button
dont: Never make purchases in an emotional state of artificial scarcity
Never save credit/debit card credentials on casual gaming or shopping websites

myths.statement: Websites display 'Only 1 left in stock!' purely as a helpful public service to alert shoppers.
myths.truth: E-commerce apps regularly code artificial countdown clocks and stock counters to trigger impulse purchases via urgency.

quiz.q: Which of the following is an example of an illegal e-commerce 'dark pattern'?
options: Displaying accurate dimensions of a backpack in centimeters
Pre-ticking a paid magazine subscription box during checkout without your consent
Showing clear return policies
Offering customer service phone numbers
quiz.explanation: Sneaking paid items into your cart via pre-ticked checkboxes is a banned dark pattern known as 'sneak into basket'.

situations: While ordering a book online at {at}, {name} notices the checkout bill increased by Rs 99 due to an auto-checked 'VIP Delivery Pass'.
scenario.question: What action should {name} take?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Spot the pre-checked dark pattern box and uncheck it to remove the unwanted fee
rubric.keys: uncheck hidden box|remove dark pattern|verify bill total

rubric.point: Carefully review every line item before approving digital payment
Complain to the platform or Consumer Helpline if hidden fees cannot be deselected

dangerous: assume added charge is mandatory government tax
save card details on untrusted site

sources.name: Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) - Dark Patterns Guidelines

cards.title: Earning your first rupee: Providing genuine value
facts: Money is earned by solving problems and delivering genuine value to people, not through luck or wishing.
Young people can build legitimate income through skills like tutoring juniors, coding basic websites, pet sitting, or crafting.
do: Identify a real skill you possess (e.g., maths tutoring, digital art, gardening) that others need
Agree on scope of work, timeline, and fair compensation upfront before starting a task
Deliver high-quality work punctually to build personal reputation and word-of-mouth trust
dont: Never take on freelance work that violates child labor protections or interferes with school attendance
Never misrepresent your qualifications or plagiarize client work

myths.statement: Making money online as a teenager only happens through viral dance videos or gaming streams.
myths.truth: Most sustainable freelance income comes from practical micro-skills like design, tutoring, transcription, and neighborhood assistance.

quiz.q: What is the fundamental basis of legitimate economic earnings?
options: Convincing people through deception
Solving a real problem and providing genuine value to others
Hoping for lottery windfalls
Borrowing without intent to repay
quiz.explanation: All enduring commerce is an exchange of value: helping someone save time, learn a skill, or solve a practical problem.

situations: During school summer holidays at {at}, {name} wants to earn money legitimately to purchase a computer course.
scenario.question: What is the most constructive approach for {name}?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Offer structured academic tutoring to neighborhood primary students in weak subjects
rubric.note: Builds service based on genuine competence.

rubric.point: Define clear hourly rates and obtain parental approval before commencing
Deliver every tutoring session punctually with prepared notes and patience

sources.name: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship

cards.title: Handling festival and shagun cash: Avoid the windfall trap
facts: Windfall cash (Diwali shagun, Eid eidi, birthday envelopes) triggers a mental accounting bias where we treat it as 'free money' to squander.
Treating gift cash with the same discipline as earned income accelerates savings goals by years.
do: Deposit at least 50% of any festival gift cash directly into long-term savings or an RD
Use a modest 25% for a meaningful personal celebration or sharing with family
Keep a personal ledger noting who gifted what so you cultivate genuine gratitude
dont: Never rush to the market within an hour of receiving gift money to spend it on impulse toys
Never brag about gift amounts to peers or compare shagun envelopes

myths.statement: Money received as a birthday or festival gift does not count as real money and should be spent instantly.
myths.truth: Gift cash has identical purchasing power to hard-earned salary; squandering it wastes prime compounding opportunities.

quiz.q: What is the smartest financial habit when receiving festival cash from grandparents?
options: Spend 100% immediately on firecrackers and candy
Allocate a significant portion to your savings fund while reserving a small portion for a treat
Hide it in a textbook and forget about it for 10 years
Hand it to strangers
quiz.explanation: Splitting windfall cash balances present celebration with meaningful asset accumulation.

situations: After family celebrations at {at}, {name} receives Rs 3,000 in cash envelopes from relatives.
scenario.question: How should {name} allocate this windfall?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Allocate at least Rs 1,500 - Rs 2,000 into a bank deposit or designated savings goal
rubric.note: Captures windfall for meaningful future utility.
rubric.keys: save 50% or more|deposit in bank|long term goal

rubric.point: Reserve a planned portion for a thoughtful personal book, game, or family treat
Thank each relative warmly with handwritten gratitude notes

cards.title: Inflation: Why 100 rupees buys less over time
facts: Inflation is the general increase in prices over time, which reduces the purchasing power of your money.
If inflation is 6% per year, an item that costs Rs 100 today will cost Rs 106 next year; cash hidden in a drawer loses value every day.
do: Understand that money sitting in physical cash loses purchasing power every year
Look for savings instruments (like PPF or mutual funds via parents) that beat inflation rates
Calculate real returns: Nominal interest rate minus inflation rate equals real wealth growth
dont: Never assume money kept in a piggy bank remains 'safe' from purchasing power erosion
Never ignore inflation when planning multi-year savings goals like college education

myths.statement: Keeping paper currency notes hidden under your mattress is the safest way to preserve your family's wealth.
myths.truth: While physical notes won't disappear, inflation steadily eats away what those notes can buy. In 15 years, their real purchasing value drops by half.

quiz.q: If a chocolate bar costs Rs 50 today and annual inflation is 6%, what will happen to the price in future years?
options: It will become free
The price will gradually increase over time
The price will decrease to Rs 10
Inflation has no effect on goods
quiz.explanation: Inflation causes the general price level of goods and services to increase over time.

situations: At home at {at}, {name} considers keeping Rs 5,000 cash in a secret metal box for five years versus depositing it into an interest-bearing bank account.
scenario.question: How should {name} reason through this decision?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Recognize that inflation will erode the purchasing power of idle paper cash over five years
rubric.keys: inflation erodes cash|purchasing power drops|idle cash loses value

rubric.point: Choose an interest-bearing bank deposit to earn returns that offset price rises
Learn to calculate real return by comparing interest rates against inflation

dangerous: assume bank interest is a scam

sources.name: Reserve Bank of India - Inflation Metrics

cards.title: Insurance basics: Protecting against financial catastrophe
facts: Insurance is a collective safety net where many people pay small regular premiums to protect against rare but devastating financial disasters.
Without health and life insurance, a single hospital emergency can wipe out an entire family's life savings and force them into predatory debt.
do: Understand that insurance is protection against catastrophic risk, not an investment to make you rich
Know the difference: Health insurance pays hospital bills; Term life insurance protects family if an earning parent passes away
Check that vehicle third-party insurance is always active before driving
dont: Never view insurance premiums as 'wasted money' just because no disaster happened this year
Never hide medical pre-existing conditions when filling insurance declaration forms

myths.statement: Buying health insurance is a complete waste of money if you stay healthy and don't visit a hospital.
myths.truth: Insurance is peace of mind against catastrophic bankruptcy. You pay a small fee so a unexpected critical illness does not ruin your family.

quiz.q: What is the primary fundamental purpose of health and life insurance?
options: To make you a stock market millionaire overnight
To protect individuals and families from catastrophic financial ruin during unforeseen emergencies
To avoid paying all municipal taxes
To borrow money without interest
quiz.explanation: Insurance pools risk to ensure unexpected medical shocks or accidents do not plunge households into poverty.

situations: During a family discussion at {at}, a relative suggests canceling family health insurance to save Rs 15,000 annual premium.
scenario.question: How can {name} explain the importance of insurance retention?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Explain that an unexpected surgery or hospital stay can cost lakhs and wipe out savings
rubric.keys: hospital emergency costs lakhs|wipes out savings|protect family

rubric.point: Clarify that insurance is a risk shield rather than a profit-making scheme
rubric.keys: risk shield not profit|peace of mind

rubric.point: Recommend comparing policy features rather than eliminating essential coverage

dangerous: assume young people never get sick

sources.name: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)

cards.title: Decoding a pay slip: Gross salary vs In-hand pay
facts: Gross salary is the total compensation promised; Net salary (in-hand) is what actually enters your bank account after mandatory deductions.
Deductions include Employee Provident Fund (EPF for retirement), Professional Tax, and Income Tax (TDS).
do: Understand that a job offering 'Rs 50,000 CTC' will not deliver Rs 50,000 cash into your account each month
Learn what EPF (Provident Fund) is: a mandatory retirement nest-egg where your employer matches your contribution
Check that your Permanent Account Number (PAN) is correctly linked to tax deductions
dont: Never sign an employment contract without examining the itemized CTC breakdown
Never ignore tax planning until the final month of the financial year

myths.statement: If a job offer letter states a salary of Rs 60,000 per month, exactly Rs 60,000 will be transferred to your bank account.
myths.truth: Gross salary undergoes statutory deductions like PF, income tax, and health insurance; net in-hand is always lower.

quiz.q: What is the crucial difference between 'Gross Salary' and 'Net Salary' on an employee pay slip?
options: There is no difference
Gross is total compensation before deductions; Net is the actual amount credited to your bank account
Gross is paid in cash, Net in coupons
Net is always double the gross amount
quiz.explanation: Net salary equals Gross salary minus statutory taxes, provident fund contributions, and insurance deductions.

situations: A young family member at {at} receives their first job offer letter boasting 'Rs 40,000 monthly CTC' but the bank transfer is Rs 33,500.
scenario.question: How can {name} help them understand their pay slip breakdown?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Review the pay slip to identify deductions like EPF retirement savings and income tax
rubric.keys: review deductions|provident fund epf|income tax tds

rubric.point: Explain that EPF deduction is not lost money, but a forced savings asset matched by the employer
rubric.keys: epf is personal retirement asset|matched by employer

rubric.point: Help verify that the Employer PAN and UAN numbers are accurately recorded

dangerous: accuse company of wage theft without reading slip

cards.title: Peer pressure spending: Confidence without designer labels
facts: Many teenagers go broke trying to impress classmates with expensive sneakers, branded cafes, and designer stationery.
True personal security and self-worth come from competence, character, and kindness—not clothing logos.
do: Practice saying comfortably: 'That's out of my budget right now, but let's hang out in the park'
Recognize that genuine friends respect your financial honesty; only shallow peers judge your clothing brands
Calculate how many hours of work or study an expensive luxury item costs before buying
dont: Never steal, borrow recklessly, or lie to your parents to keep up with wealthy peers' spending
Never look down on classmates who carry simple cloth bags or homemade lunchboxes

myths.statement: Wearing expensive designer brands is the only proven way to earn genuine respect and popularity in school.
myths.truth: Brand obsession signals insecurity. Real leadership, warmth, athletic or artistic skill, and wit command far greater respect.

quiz.q: What is the most emotionally mature response when friends suggest an expensive cafe you cannot afford?
options: Lie that you already ate, then secretly borrow money
Confidently state: 'That place is outside my budget, how about we grab street chai or hang in the library?'
Insult your friends for being rich
Steal money from your parents' wallet
quiz.explanation: Owning your budget with calm confidence earns peer respect and prevents toxic debt traps.

situations: At school at {at}, {name}'s friend group plans a weekend outing to an upscale restaurant with Rs 1,000 per head cover charge, which exceeds {name}'s allowance.
scenario.question: What is the best course of action for {name}?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: State calmly and without shame that the restaurant exceeds your current budget
Propose an affordable alternative or offer to join them afterwards for a walk in the park
Refuse to pressure parents into funding non-essential luxury outings
rubric.keys: do not pressure parents|protect family budget

dangerous: lie and make up fake illnesses

sources.name: National Mental Health Programme - Life Skills Education

cards.title: In-app gaming traps: Microtransactions and loot boxes
facts: Free-to-play mobile games are engineered by behavioral psychologists to trigger dopamine loops and loot-box gambling addictions.
Microtransactions of 'just Rs 49' accumulate into thousands of rupees drained from linked parental cards within days.
do: Never link your parent's UPI or credit card directly to Google Play or Apple App Store without biometric confirmation
Understand that virtual weapon skins and character outfits have zero real-world resale value
Set a hard monthly cap of Rs 0 on randomized loot boxes, treating them as gambling mechanisms
dont: NEVER secretly use a parent's phone to authorize gaming purchases
NEVER fall for third-party websites promising 'free diamonds' or 'unlimited game coins' in exchange for account logins

myths.statement: Loot boxes in mobile games are completely harmless games of skill.
myths.truth: Loot boxes employ variable-ratio reinforcement schedules identical to slot machines, creating addictive spending spirals.

quiz.q: Why do mobile games convert real currency into virtual gems, diamonds, or coins before you purchase items?
options: To comply with international space law
To psychologically detach you from the feeling of spending real rupee money
Because banks cannot process rupees
To give away free bonuses
quiz.explanation: Virtual tokens obscure real-world monetary value, making gamers spend far more impulsively.

situations: While playing a mobile battle-royale game at {at}, {name} is tempted to spend Rs 799 on a limited-time legendary weapon skin using a parent's pre-linked payment profile.
scenario.question: What should {name} do?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Stop and recognize that virtual game skins deliver zero real-world value and will be obsolete in months
rubric.keys: virtual skin has zero value|game trap|resist urge

rubric.point: Always ask explicit parental permission before making any digital purchase
Advise removing saved payment methods to avoid accidental one-click debits
rubric.keys: remove saved card|disable one click pay

dangerous: secretly click purchase hoping parents wont notice

cards.title: SMART financial goals: Turning dreams into savings plans
facts: Vague goals like 'I want to save money' fail; SMART financial goals (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound) succeed.
Breaking a Rs 2,400 bicycle repair target into Rs 200 saved per month over 12 months makes huge goals easily achievable.
do: Write down the exact item, total cost, target date, and required weekly savings amount
Create a visual progress tracker (thermometer chart or checklist) on your study desk
Celebrate reaching 25%, 50%, and 75% milestones without spending the accumulated corpus
dont: Never leave your savings goals abstract without a written number and deadline
Never abandon a goal just because an unexpected expense slowed your progress by two weeks

myths.statement: Writing down your savings goals makes no measurable difference to whether you achieve them.
myths.truth: Studies in behavioral economics show written, visual goal tracking increases savings completion rates by over 40%

quiz.q: Which of the following represents a properly structured 'SMART' financial goal?
options: 'I want to be rich someday'
'I will save Rs 300 every month for 6 months to buy a Rs 1,800 science telescope by December'
'I will stop spending money forever'
'I hope someone gifts me a computer'
quiz.explanation: It includes a specific item, exact target amount, defined monthly saving rate, and a clear deadline.

situations: {name} dreams of buying a Rs 1,200 scientific calculator for class 11 at {at} in four months.
scenario.question: How should {name} organize this savings plan?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Calculate the required rate: Rs 1,200 divided by 4 months equals Rs 300 per month (Rs 75/week)
rubric.keys: divide 1200 by 4 months|300 per month|75 per week

rubric.point: Set up a dedicated physical envelope or digital sub-wallet labeled 'Calculator Fund'
Track progress weekly in a notebook to ensure discipline until the goal is achieved

dangerous: wait until exam day and borrow money
give up because 1200 feels too big
